body:
Helium is a fiction city on Mars, in the imagined world called Barsoom, and it is presented here as fiction, never as fact. In the stories it is formed from two twin cities, Greater Helium and Lesser Helium, joined as one state, and it is known for its towers, its airships, and its place as a leading power of that imagined Mars.

Helium's people, in the stories, travel by air and by canal-side roads, and the city is organized around palaces, gardens, and harbors for its flying craft. Nothing in this record claims that Helium exists on the real planet Mars, and no passage from the books is quoted here.

Planet

Planet: Mars (Barsoom, in fiction).

Honesty label

FICTION. Source work: the Barsoom books of Edgar Rice Burroughs. This record is an original summary, not a reproduction of the books.

Districts

  • Twin city cores (Greater and Lesser Helium): palaces, government halls, and the joined heart of the state
  • Tower districts: tall residential and lookout towers above the city streets
  • Airship harbors: docking and repair yards for the flying craft of the stories
  • Garden quarters: planted courts and public gardens between the towers
  • Canal-side markets: trade streets along the waterways of imagined Barsoom

Ecosystems

  • Dry canal plains around the city
  • thin-air sky used by airships
  • desert borderlands beyond the walls
  • garden microclimates inside the city courts

Caves / Underground

Caves and underground: no caves appear in the source material for Helium, so the underground treatment is stated explicitly: foundations, cellars, and service passages beneath the towers, plus water cisterns fed by the canals. No hidden cave system is claimed.

title: Luna City
description: Luna City is a theorized settlement on the Moon, and this record treats it as a proposal, not an existing place. The name has been used for proposed lunar towns and for fictional Moon cities, and this record keeps those two uses separate: the proposal is engineering, the fiction is story.
body:
Luna City is a theorized settlement on the Moon, and this record treats it as a proposal, not an existing place. The name has been used for proposed lunar towns and for fictional Moon cities, and this record keeps those two uses separate: the proposal is engineering, the fiction is story.

A real Luna City would have to solve air, water, radiation, and temperature before any street could be lived on. Its districts would therefore be pressurized habitats first and civic spaces second, with every outdoor movement planned through airlocks and shielded routes.

Planet

Planet: the Moon (Earth's Moon).

Honesty label

THEORIZED. Status: a proposed lunar settlement name, used in planning discussions and in fiction. No such city exists on the Moon today.

Districts

  • Pressurized habitat ring: linked living modules with air, water, and power
  • Airlock and transit hub: suited and pressurized movement in and out of the habitats
  • Workshop and repair district: maintenance, fabrication, and vehicle servicing
  • Greenhouse quarter: food growth under artificial light and recycled water
  • Observatory rise: telescopes and communications on high ground

Ecosystems

  • Airless lunar surface and regolith plains
  • crater rim highlands
  • permanently shadowed cold traps near the poles
  • the black sky above, with Earth visible

Caves / Underground

Caves and underground: the underground treatment is the lunar lava-tube option, stated as a proposal, not a found city: natural tubes, if confirmed at a site, could be sealed and pressurized as shielded halls, joined to surface habitats by airlocked tunnels. Where no tube is confirmed, the underground is buried habitat modules under regolith shielding.

It is theorized and planned, not built, and every claim here is about proposals and engineering needs, not about an existing city.

The south-polar site matters because sunlight on high ground and water ice in shadowed craters are both proposed resources. A base there would grow by adding habitat modules, power units, and landing pads, with each addition tested before the next is occupied.

  • Power ridge: solar arrays on sunlit high ground plus stored power
  • Ice prospecting field: survey and test extraction in nearby shadowed craters
  • Rover garage and routes: pressurized and unpressurized vehicles and marked surface routes

  • Sunlit polar highlands
  • permanently shadowed crater floors
  • regolith plains and ridges
  • the airless sky and the Earth in view

Caves / Underground

Caves and underground: no caves are claimed for Artemis. The underground treatment is explicit: buried and bermed modules for radiation shielding, plus cable and pipe trenches, and survey tunnels only if a lava tube or ice deposit is confirmed by measurement. title: Terminus
description: Terminus is a fiction city-planet settlement, and it is presented here as fiction, never as fact. In the stories it is a small, resource-poor world at the galaxy's edge, chosen as the home of the Encyclopedia Foundation, and its single city grows from that scholarly start into a trading power.
body:
Terminus is a fiction city-planet settlement, and it is presented here as fiction, never as fact. In the stories it is a small, resource-poor world at the galaxy's edge, chosen as the home of the Encyclopedia Foundation, and its single city grows from that scholarly start into a trading power.

Terminus City's imagined plan starts with the Foundation's halls and libraries, then adds a spaceport, markets, and workshops as trade grows. This record follows that growth in order, simple settlement first, trading city later, and keeps it all inside fiction.

Planet

Planet: Terminus (a planet at the edge of the galaxy, in fiction).

Honesty label

FICTION. Source work: the Foundation stories of Isaac Asimov. This record is an original summary, not a reproduction of any book.

Districts

  • Foundation halls: the encyclopedia project, libraries, and schools of the stories
  • Spaceport and trade quarter: landings, warehouses, and merchant halls
  • Workshop and power district: manufacture, repair, and the city's power works
  • Residential town: homes for scholars, traders, and workers
  • Observatory hill: the observatory and signal station of the stories

Ecosystems

  • Rocky coastline and thin soils of Terminus in the stories
  • the edge-of-galaxy sky
  • sea and harbor approaches
  • the barren interior beyond the city

Caves / Underground

Caves and underground: no caves are a feature of Terminus City in the source material, so the underground treatment is stated explicitly: foundations, archives below the Foundation halls, cellars, and service tunnels for power and water. No hidden cave city is claimed.

total_km = 0.0

print("Total distance: %.1f km, total time: %.2f hours" % (total_km, total_h))

body:
Arrakeen is a fiction city on the planet Arrakis, and it is presented here as fiction, never as fact. In the stories it is the capital of a desert planet where water is precious, spice is the great trade good, and the city is built to shelter its people from the deep desert.

Arrakeen's imagined plan is a walled desert capital: a palace and residency quarter, shielded streets, markets for spice and water trade, and landing fields beyond the walls. This record describes that plan in original words and quotes nothing from the novels.

Planet

Planet: Arrakis.

Honesty label

FICTION. Source work: the Dune novels of Frank Herbert. This record is an original summary, not a reproduction of any book.

Districts

  • Residency and palace quarter: the governor's residency and government halls of the stories
  • Shielded market streets: spice, water, and craft trade under cover
  • Water discipline quarter: cisterns, recycling, and water discipline of the stories
  • Landing fields: arrivals and departures beyond the walls
  • Worker and sietch-gate districts: homes and the gates toward the desert people of the stories

Ecosystems

  • Deep desert and dunes beyond the walls
  • rocky shield-wall highlands
  • the harsh sun and dry sky
  • oasis and garden enclaves inside the walls, watered at great cost in the stories

Caves / Underground

Caves and underground: the underground treatment is stated explicitly: in the stories, the desert people live in sietch caves in the rock, and Arrakeen's record gives the city cisterns, cellars, and service tunnels beneath its streets, plus the sietch cave systems beyond the walls, described only in summary. Those caves belong to the fiction, not to any real desert.

title: Coruscant
description: Coruscant is a fiction planet-city, and it is presented here as fiction, never as fact. In the stories the whole planet is one city, stacked thousands of levels high, and it was the capital of a republic and then an empire.
body:
Coruscant is a fiction planet-city, and it is presented here as fiction, never as fact. In the stories the whole planet is one city, stacked thousands of levels high, and it was the capital of a republic and then an empire.

Coruscant's imagined plan stacks government, commerce, housing, industry, and the undercity in vertical layers, with traffic lanes in the sky between the towers. This record gives the overview in plain summary and leaves the ranked building options to the coruscant-blueprints pair.

Planet

Districts

  • Senate and government district: the senate, courts, and government towers of the stories
  • Commerce and entertainment levels: shops, theaters, and trade halls stacked in the towers
  • Residential levels: homes from sunlit upper levels to dim middle levels
  • Industrial and power levels: works, docks, and power systems deep in the stack
  • Undercity levels: the lowest levels, where sunlight never reaches in the stories

Those levels are imagined, and no real planet-city is claimed.

title: Mars City States
description: Mars City States is a theorized idea: a group of Martian settlements that govern themselves and federate with one another, rather than a single capital ruling the planet. It is a proposal about how future settlements might organize, not a description of anything on Mars today.
body:
Mars City States is a theorized idea: a group of Martian settlements that govern themselves and federate with one another, rather than a single capital ruling the planet. It is a proposal about how future settlements might organize, not a description of anything on Mars today.

The idea grows step by step: first one pressurized outpost, then several outposts in different regions, then trade and shared rules between them, then a federation of city-states. Each step depends on life support, radiation shielding, and transport being proven at the previous step, and no step is presented as already achieved.

Planet

Planet: Mars.

Honesty label

THEORIZED. Status: a proposed federation of Martian settlements, theorized and not existing. No Martian city exists today.

Cross-link

Cross-link: future-mars-city-states — the existing cousin database on Martian settlement concepts; this record is the any-planet family overview and cross-links to it, not a rebuild of it.

Districts

  • Elysium outpost (proposed): a first settlement district in a low, sheltered region
  • Tharsis industrial district (proposed): workshops, power, and fabrication for the federation
  • Polar research town (proposed): ice and science work at the poles
  • Canyon greenhouse belt (proposed): food growth in sheltered canyon sites
  • Federation assembly hall (proposed): the shared council chamber of the city-states

Ecosystems

  • Martian plains and volcanoes
  • canyon systems
  • polar ice caps
  • the thin Martian sky

Caves / Underground

Caves and underground: the underground treatment is stated explicitly and as a proposal: Martian lava tubes, if confirmed at a chosen site, could shelter settlements from radiation, joined by airlocked tunnels; where no tube is confirmed, settlements are buried modules under regolith. No Martian cave city is claimed to exist.
